FilePath.description: Repository-relative file path. May contain `/` separators, which are sent literally.
FilePath.name: path

IdempotencyKey.description: Caller-chosen key that makes a retry the same request. A UUID is what every first-party client sends and what the documentation recommends, but the runtime stores and compares the value as opaque text, so the contract does not impose a format the server does not enforce — a non-UUID key was accepted by the Spark and rejected by contract validation.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

PresenceKeyProof.description: Unpadded base64url raw P-256 r||s signature by the proposed presence key over SPARK-PRESENCE-ENROLL2, bound to the authenticated method, path/query, timestamp, nonce, content digest, device ID, and canonical presence-key fingerprint and trusted recipient node UUID.
PresenceKeyProof.name: X-Spark-Presence-Key-Proof

PreviewPath.description: Path within the previewed service. May contain `/` separators, which are sent literally.
PreviewPath.name: path

RequiredUserPresence.description: Unpadded base64url of a compact JSON object containing version 2, an RFC3339 expires_at no more than 60 seconds after both the SPARK2 timestamp and server verification time, and a raw P-256 signature. The signature uses the separately registered presence key and canonical scheme SPARK-PRESENCE2.
RequiredUserPresence.name: X-Spark-User-Presence

SparkContentSha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the request body, empty-string digest when there is no body. Binds the signature to the bytes sent.
SparkContentSha256.name: X-Spark-Content-Sha256

SparkDeviceId.description: The paired device making the request.
SparkDeviceId.name: X-Spark-Device-Id

SparkNodeId.description: Trusted paired recipient node UUID, which must equal the receiving runtime identity and is signed as the final SPARK2 canonical line.
SparkNodeId.name: X-Spark-Node-ID

SparkNonce.description: Single-use value, unique per device, that makes a captured request unreplayable within the timestamp window.
SparkNonce.name: X-Spark-Nonce

SparkTimestamp.description: RFC 3339 instant the request was signed. The runtime refuses anything outside a 120-second window in either direction.
SparkTimestamp.name: X-Spark-Timestamp

UserPresence.description: Conditionally required proof using the same compact JSON and SPARK-PRESENCE2 scheme as RequiredUserPresence.
UserPresence.name: X-Spark-User-Presence

capacity_released.description: Capacity is free only after terminal backend evidence or confirmed owned-engine termination; an unknown output may remain unknown

instructions.description: What the owner asked the Spark to do, sent to the model as the task.

last_run_state.description: The state of the most recent run, or `none` when the automation has not run yet.

next_run_at.description: Absolute Unix seconds of the next slot, computed on the Spark in the automation's zone.

web_access.description: Whether this automation may search the web and read pages. Off unless the owner turned it on.

notify.description: Send a notification to every paired device when a run finishes. Run history is always kept.

web_access.description: Defaults to false. Turning it on requires a fresh user-presence proof because it changes what the Spark sends to third parties.

scheduled_for.description: The slot this run belongs to, absent for Run now.

expression.description: Five cron fields — minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week — accepting `*`, a number, a comma list, an inclusive range and `*/N`. Every preset is stored as an ordinary expression.

preset.description: How the app composed the expression. `custom` means the owner typed one.

timezone.description: IANA zone the expression is read in, for example `Europe/London`. Stored with the automation so a Spark in another zone still fires at the owner's local time.

outcome.description: A client must render an outcome it does not know generically rather than as a refusal.

query.description: The exact search text that left the Spark, recorded so the owner can read it back.

url.description: The final URL after redirects, or the URL that was refused.

AutomationUpdateRequest.description: Only the supplied fields change. An absent field is left as it is.

ConfigureRemoteOverlayRequest.description: Change exactly one preference; preserve all other Tailscale settings and account membership.

access_authentication.description: Absent on older API v1 runtimes.

server_observed_transport.description: The runtime has no trusted ingress binding and therefore does not guess LAN, Wi-Fi, or overlay transport.

CreateSharedAccessInvitation.description: The limits for one shared-access invitation, plus how long the link should live.

invitation_expires_in_seconds.description: Defaults to seven days, the maximum for a shared-access link.

DiagnosticsExclusion.description: Content no control can include, and why. Clients must not present an exclusion as a category the owner could enable.

include_optional.description: Ids of optional categories the owner ticked for this export. An id the runtime does not offer is refused rather than ignored.

DiagnosticsFile.description: One UTF-8 text entry. `content` is a JSON document the owner can read before sharing it.

DiagnosticsManifest.description: Every file in the bundle with its sensitivity class, plus what was left out. Derived from the produced files, so a file without a manifest entry cannot exist.

DiagnosticsSection.description: One part of the support bundle, described before it is produced.

sensitivity.description: `operational` names no person, address or secret. `identifying` describes this owner's installation and is only ever produced when the owner asks for it.

GuestDaySchedule.description: One weekday's allowed blocks, in the owner's time zone. Monday is 0.

GuestHourWindow.description: One block of allowed local time. start_minute is inclusive, end_minute is exclusive, and 1440 means local midnight.

GuestSchedule.description: A guest's allowed hours for the whole week, always read in the owner's time zone.

GuestUsage.description: What one guest used over a period of local days.

auth_protocols.description: Request-signing protocols this runtime accepts. An app that speaks none of them must update itself or the runtime before requests can succeed.

HouseholdNoteRequest.description: Create with revision zero; editing and deleting require the last observed revision. Deleted note text is purged; id and revision remain to reject stale writes.

Identity.description: `authority_fingerprint` identifies the Ed25519 authority that signs pairing material. `tls_fingerprint` is SHA-256 of the exact leaf certificate DER served by the local API. The values are independent and must never be substituted for one another.

tls_fingerprint.description: Null only in explicit development-only plain HTTP mode.

availability.description: unsupported means this runtime recognises the engine but has no verified parser for its metrics. unavailable means a supported endpoint could not produce a bounded sample.

server_queue_ms.description: Engine queue timing is not reported by this collector

last_unload.description: Evidence from the most recent stop while nothing is loaded; null once a model is loaded again.

adopt_existing.description: Connect the existing Open WebUI container at this port without changing its accounts, configuration or data

port.description: Local service port; omission retains the managed default 18080

publisher.description: Who published the model weights (the recipe's metadata.publisher).

recipe_source.description: Who wrote the serving recipe, as distinct from who published the model.

ModelActionPreviewAlternativeProfile.description: A profile of the same signed recipe that the current memory budget would admit, so a refusal can name a concrete smaller context instead of asking the owner to go and find one.

alternative_profiles.description: Present when a memory blocker refused the requested profile. Lists profiles of the same recipe that the current budget admits, smallest peak first, so the client can offer a named alternative. Empty means nothing on this recipe fits the current budget.

max_context_now.description: Largest context, rounded down to a multiple of 4096 tokens, that fits at the profile's request count after the system reserve, weights, overhead and per-request state.

max_sequences_now.description: Requests that fit at the profile's full context, bounded by the engine policy.

idle_timeout_seconds.description: Optional custom idle timeout for a timed unload policy; overrides its named duration. Omit to use the named duration. Not valid with keep_ready or manual_only.
Saved custom timeout overriding the named timed idle policy, when present.

supports_custom_idle_timeout.description: True only when this runtime and engine accept a custom idle_timeout_seconds setting.

valid_for_milliseconds.description: Measure freshness with the receiver monotonic clock after receipt; never trust sender wall-clock age.

configuration_state.description: Whether a credential-free, loopback-only OpenAI model-list probe established the external engine configuration. unavailable never means that no model is served.

management_origin.description: Why a managed workload is in SparkPilot's lifecycle. Null for every externally managed workload.

adopted.description: Existing container connected without lifecycle authority

ownership_verified.description: Trusted privileged ownership evidence matches the exact current container and data volume

repair_available.description: A bounded repair is available without starting an intentionally stopped service

presence_key_signature.description: Required when presence_public_key_spki is present and forbidden when it is absent. The presence key signs the same SPARK-PAIRING-PRESENCE1 registration message as the normal device key challenge signature.

presence_public_key_spki.description: Optional distinct P-256 SPKI for fresh user-presence proofs. Devices paired without this field remain compatible but cannot authorize device revocation.

presence_key_fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the canonical uncompressed SEC1 P-256 presence public key accepted by the runtime. A client that requested registration must require this value to match its local key.

join_code.description: Short-lived code for adding another local Apple device.

node_name.description: Version 2. The Spark's name, signed so a link cannot claim to be another Spark.

remote_hostname.description: Version 2. The Spark's MagicDNS name, present only when remote access is enabled.

shared_access.description: Version 2. The guest limits this invitation grants.

tls_fingerprint.description: Version 2. The TLS leaf pin the joining device must see.

harness_updates.description: Prepared coding agents with a newer version pinned by this signed runtime; opening a new session prepares the update without stopping existing work.

overlay_setup_state.description: The Tailscale client state the review found when it would set the overlay up rather than reuse an enrolled route.

accept_dns.description: Whether the Spark accepts DNS configuration from its tailnet.

enabled.description: The Spark's saved VPN preference; this does not prove this Apple device can reach it.

address.description: The node's 100.64/10 Tailscale address once signed in.

authorization_url.description: The owner's one-time browser sign-in link, always on the login.tailscale.com origin; present only while a one-tap enable is waiting for it.

detail.description: The helper's own reason for an unavailable or stopped state.

hostname.description: The node's MagicDNS name once signed in (for example spark-example.tail1234.ts.net).

installable.description: When not_installed, whether the runtime can install the vendor package itself.

state.description: What the Spark's own Tailscale client needs before the private route can exist.

tailnet.description: The MagicDNS suffix of the tailnet the Spark joined.

private_overlay_address.description: The live 100.64/10 address beside the published hostname, which is the MagicDNS name when the Spark's Tailscale client reports one.

request_id.description: UUIDv7 logical request identity. New requests must be at most 120 seconds old and at most 5 seconds ahead of the node clock. Known exact receipts are recovered before the age gate. Terminal or proven-stopped receipts expire after 10 minutes; old IDs remain inadmissible after retirement. Unknown attempts still holding capacity never expire by age alone.

endpoint.description: Owner-approved numeric on-link HTTPS origin; no hostnames, credentials, path, query, fragment, redirects or proxy.

SharedAccessGuest.description: One guest as the owner's Shared access screen shows it.

device_id.description: Null until the friend has joined.

refusals_this_week.description: Refusals over the last seven local days, counted by error code.

SharedAccessInvitation.description: A signed shared-access invitation and the trust material the friend's app pins.

remote_hostname.description: The Spark's MagicDNS name, present only when remote access is enabled.

SharedAccessLimits.description: What the owner decided one guest may do. An empty allowed_models list permits nothing.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds after which the guest's access stops working.

time_zone.description: An IANA zone name the Spark can resolve, such as Europe/London.

SharedAccessSelf.description: What one guest may read about its own access. It never names another device.

budget_resets_at.description: Unix seconds of the next local midnight in the owner's time zone.

SharedAccessState.description: Where a guest's access is in its lifecycle. Only active can run inference.

SharedAccessSummary.description: The limits carried inside a signed shared-access invitation, so the friend can read them before joining and nobody can alter them on the way.

input.description: Also bounded to 12000 UTF-8 bytes by the runtime.

thermal_critical_celsius.description: Configured entry threshold for `critical`, at which the guard asks the engine to unload.

thermal_hot_celsius.description: Configured entry threshold for `hot`, at which the guard stops admitting new load work.

thermal_state.description: The guard's own sustained-heat rung (§41.5.2.1). `unavailable` means no memory guard is running and `unknown` means it is running with no temperature reading; an absent member means a runtime older than this field, which a client treats as `unavailable`. Clients present this rather than deriving a verdict from `temperature_celsius`, which carries no thresholds.

thermal_warning_celsius.description: Configured entry threshold for `warm`; null when no guard is running.

latest_observed_at.description: The newest bucket recorded, or null when there is none.

recording.description: Whether the runtime is recording. False means functional telemetry consent is off, and an empty `rows` then means "not recorded" rather than "nothing happened".

memory_pressure.description: One of normal, warning, critical or emergency, or absent.

sample_count.description: How many ten-second samples this row represents.

engines.description: Loopback-only Prometheus observations for SparkPilot-managed and recognised external engines. Counters remain on this Spark and unavailable readings are null rather than fabricated as zero.

memory_psi_full_avg10.description: Linux memory PSI full-stall percentage averaged over the preceding 10 seconds, or null when unavailable

memory_psi_some_avg10.description: Linux memory PSI partial-stall percentage averaged over the preceding 10 seconds, or null when unavailable

thermal_critical_celsius.description: Configured entry threshold for `critical`, at which the guard asks the engine to unload.

thermal_hot_celsius.description: Configured entry threshold for `hot`, at which the guard stops admitting new load work.

thermal_state.description: The guard's own sustained-heat rung (§41.5.2.1). `unavailable` means no memory guard is running and `unknown` means it is running with no temperature reading; an absent member means a runtime older than this field, which a client treats as `unavailable`. Clients present this rather than deriving a verdict from `temperature_celsius`, which carries no thresholds.

thermal_warning_celsius.description: Configured entry threshold for `warm`; null when no guard is running.

instruction.description: What the model should do with the text.

source_name.description: Display label for the analysed document. Not a path, and never used to open anything.

target.description: The identity the caller believes it is addressing. A mismatch is refused with TARGET_IDENTITY_MISMATCH rather than answered.

text.description: The extracted document text. The caller extracts it; this endpoint never opens a file and never receives a path.

UnloadEvidence.description: What the most recent engine stop found about unified memory. memory_recovered false means the engine stopped but memory did not return to its pre-load baseline within the recovery timeout.

UpdateDevice.description: Capabilities are derived from the role by the runtime's capability matrix (§61) and are not settable per device; a capability list here would be accepted and ignored, which reads as success.

UpdateSharedAccess.description: Confirm, pause or re-limit one guest. Withdrawing access has its own route.

UsageTelemetry.description: Today's accounting, in UTC. Exact for the requests it covers, and it covers a narrower set than "everything this Spark served": only requests SparkPilot itself mediated, that completed, that reported usage, and that ran while functional telemetry consent was enabled. Requests served directly by an engine, or that failed before reporting usage, are not here. See docs/operations/telemetry-accounting.md.

failures.description: Null when this runtime does not account for failures, which it currently does not. Null means "not counted"; zero would mean "none happened", which this build cannot establish.

requests.description: Completed SparkPilot-mediated requests that reported usage.

due_at.description: Absolute Unix seconds on the Spark clock; one minute to seven days ahead at review. The reviewed schedule may be accepted until one second before its due time.

allow_domains.description: When non-empty, only these domains and their subdomains may be read.

brave_credential_id.description: Reference to a stored `brave-search` provider credential. The key itself never leaves the Spark.

deny_domains.description: Always refused, even inside an allowed domain.

harness_access.description: Whether third-party clients on the OpenAI-compatible gateway may also use the web tools. Off unless the owner turned it on, and only meaningful when the policy allows chats.

local_search_state.description: Whether the Spark's own search service is installed and answering. Choosing the `searxng` backend at the Spark's own address installs it as part of the same operation.

policy.description: What the owner has allowed the model to reach. `off` until an owner changes it; the per-automation and per-chat opt-ins sit on top and never override it.

search_backend.description: Which search service the Spark asks. `searxng` is the default and points at the Spark's own instance, so a query carries no account identity. `disabled` leaves page reading available and refuses every search.

searxng_url.description: Base URL of the owner's own SearXNG, used only when the backend is `searxng`.

truncated.description: True when the answer stopped at the token ceiling rather than finishing.

system_instruction.description: Prepended ahead of the web-tool contract, so another surface can add its own framing without replacing the untrusted-content rule.

WorkloadEngine.description: The engine this workload was recognised as from bounded facts. `none` means recognition did not succeed, not that no engine is present.

WorkloadOwnership.description: Ownership state from the master specification section 29.6. spark_managed means Spark Runtime owns the durable lifecycle; external_observed means the workload was recognised but is never sent a lifecycle command; adoption_available means a signed recipe matches closely enough to build a preview; unknown_external means the workload consumes resources but could not be identified safely.

SparkDeviceSignature.description: Part of a multi-header P-256 request-signing scheme. `X-Spark-Signature` carries the signature; the canonical string it signs also requires `X-Spark-Node-ID`, `X-Spark-Device-Id`, `X-Spark-Timestamp`, `X-Spark-Nonce` and `X-Spark-Content-Sha256` on every request, declared as the `SparkNodeId`, `SparkDeviceId`, `SparkTimestamp`, `SparkNonce` and `SparkContentSha256` parameters below. A request missing any of them cannot be verified and is refused.
SparkDeviceSignature.name: X-Spark-Signature

post.description: The client sends a randomized 32-byte BoringSSL-compatible SPAKE2 Alice share, never the code. Both sides use SHA-256 of spark-pairing-join-code-v1: followed by the six ASCII digits as the password, with identities SparkPilot pairing v2 client and SparkPilot pairing v2 server. The response seals a PairingJoinPackage using AES-256-GCM, a key derived as SHA-256 of spark-pairing-seal-v2 followed by the 64-byte SPAKE2 key, and spark-pairing-seal-v2 as additional authenticated data. The combined value contains a 12-byte nonce, ciphertext and 16-byte tag. Before claiming, the client must match the sealed certificate fingerprint to the TLS peer. Each exchange consumes the node-wide 60-attempt/15-minute budget. Only the newest pending invitation is selected; issuing a new one changes the active code. Claims still enforce expiry, revocation and one-time consumption.
